name: RESULTS
markdown:
## What the results show

- **Invasive carcinoma is separated well from the other classes on the test split.** Invasive-vs-rest AUROC is 0.998 [0.994, 1.000], invasive sensitivity is 1.000 [1.000, 1.000] and specificity is 0.970 [0.936, 1.000]. These come from n = 132 images in 24 patient or pseudo-patient groups. No invasive case was called in situ (0 of 31), but 3 of 30 in situ cases were called invasive. In practice the model over-calls in situ disease as invasive more often than it misses invasive disease.
- **The four-class task is less certain.** Macro-F1 is 0.83 [0.61, 0.93], balanced accuracy 0.84 [0.62, 0.94] and macro AUROC 0.947 [0.852, 0.992]. The lower bounds near 0.6 reflect only 24 groups. Grouped cross-validation inside train gave a macro-F1 of 0.951 [0.915, 0.980] (n 218, 49 groups), so the test split is clearly harder than training.
- **Performance is close to published THUNDER linear probes, but the comparison is not like-for-like.** Ours is 83.0 [60.9, 92.7] macro-F1; published probes are UNI2-h 84.7 and CONCH 84.4, with no CI. The split is the same, but the protocol differs: published probes resize the whole image, while we use tiles plus test-time augmentation. This is an anchor, not a ranking.
- **The concept-bottleneck model nearly matches on invasive detection but loses on four classes.** On invasive-vs-rest AUROC, `cb_text` minus the production model is 0.00 [-0.01, 0.00]. On four-class macro-F1, `cb_text` gets 70.8 versus 83.0. Using concepts as the decision layer costs about 12 macro-F1 points in this run.
- **In simulation, triage speeds up invasive reads at a stated cost.** Mean time to first look at an invasive case falls from 20.2 to 6.0 minutes, a difference of -14.2 [-51.3, 0.0]. Unflagged cases wait 25.0 [0.7, 93.2] minutes longer. This is a 1000-day simulation with a fixed 9-minute read time, not a measured workflow outcome.

## Is the confidence trustworthy?

**Calibration: not shown to improve.** Temperature scaling (T = 0.501, fit on train out-of-fold predictions) gave mixed results. ECE was computed with 10 equal-mass bins, which is biased at this sample size.

| | Before | After | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| ECE | 0.10 [0.07, 0.19] | 0.05 [0.04, 0.22] | Point estimate halves, but the upper CI bound rises |
| Brier | 0.28 [0.14, 0.47] | 0.27 [0.11, 0.53] | No meaningful change |
| NLL | 0.56 [0.29, 1.00] | 0.66 [0.20, 1.56] | Worse |

A temperature below 1 sharpens the probabilities. Higher NLL suggests the remaining errors became more confident. A plausible cause is that the temperature was fit on training out-of-fold predictions, where the model is much more accurate than on test. With n = 132 the intervals overlap heavily, so the honest summary is that calibration was not shown to improve.

**Conformal prediction: the pre-registered method failed its target; the method now in use was chosen after seeing test results.** The target coverage is 90% (alpha 0.1).

| Method | Coverage | Mean set size | Empty sets | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lac_marginal` | 72.7% [60.7%, 84.4%] | 0.81 | 18.9% | Pre-registered; misses the target |
| `mondrian` | 53.0% [38.7%, 73.6%] | 0.61 | 39.4% | Misses badly |
| `aps` | 87.9% [73.7%, 95.7%] | 1.29 | 2.3% | |
| `aps_marginal_nonempty` | 90.2% [75.7%, 98.1%] | 1.31 | 0.0% | Used for tiers; chosen post hoc |

- The report gives a likely cause for the failure. The 50-image calibration split is far easier than the test split, which probably violates the exchangeability that the guarantee requires.
- The switch to `aps_marginal_nonempty` was made after viewing test results. Its 90.2% coverage is therefore optimistic and does not independently confirm anything. Separately, the 90% guarantee is marginal over calibration sets; it is not a guarantee for this cohort. Under the stated assumptions, conditional coverage is about Beta(46, 5) (SD 0.041).
- Per-class coverage of the tier set is uneven: Normal 82.6% (n 23), Benign 87.5% (n 48), InSitu 90.0% (n 30), Invasive 100.0% (n 31). Normal, Benign and InSitu each come from only 6 groups. Per-class coverage of the pre-registered LAC set was much lower: 56.5%, 70.8%, 66.7% and 93.5%.
- Mean set size of 1.31 means most cases get a single label. The sets give a differential on only a minority of cases.

**Reliability and deferral: these signals are weak.**

- The error detector has an AUROC of 0.70 [0.59, 0.86]. Error recall is 0.46 [0.29, 0.61], so the flag catches fewer than half of errors. The evaluation covers n = 1716 cases but still only 24 groups.
- Signal by signal:
  - Conformal set size: AUROC 0.70 [0.64, 0.79]
  - CONCH–MUSK disagreement: AUROC 0.61 [0.51, 0.75]
  - Out-of-distribution percentile: AUROC 0.49 [0.40, 0.58], which is chance. That signal contributes nothing as measured.
- Accuracy under degradation drops from 0.84 to about 0.69–0.70 at the mildest level of blur, JPEG compression, stain change and resampling. It does not keep falling at higher levels: it ranges from 0.67 to 0.74 across levels 1–3. The CIs are wide.
- No abstention curve (accuracy against deferral rate) is reported. Whether deferring improves the accuracy of the cases that are kept is untested.

**Simulated margin read: specific but insensitive.**

- On benign images, the false tumor-at-margin rate is 0.0% (284 margins, 7 groups). The threshold is very high: P = 0.99982 [0.84738, 0.99989].
- Of carcinoma images, 47.5% [25.0%, 64.7%] have at least one margin called clear.
- On annotated WSI windows, sensitivity is 45.4% [25.4%, 65.2%] and specificity 98.5% [96.7%, 100.0%].
- In composite fields, 40.0% of carcinoma-half segments exceed the threshold.
- All margins are simulated: image borders stand in for inked margins.

## Does the interpretability hold up?

A fluent explanation is not evidence of what the model used. Only the deletion test asks whether the production model depends on the highlighted regions. Everything else measures association or plausibility.

| Explanation | Test | Result | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Region risk heatmap (`uni2h_lr`) | Deletion compared with random | Top-risk minus random: 0.02 [0.00, 0.05] on predicted-aggressive cases (n 34, 17 groups); 0.01 [0.00, 0.02] on all cases (n 132) | Passes narrowly. The effect is small and the lower bound touches 0. |
| Concept attributions (`uni2h_lr`) | Deletion compared with random | Concept minus random: 0.00 [-0.02, 0.01] (n 34) and 0.00 [-0.01, 0.01] (n 132) | Fails. Removing top-concept regions changes the output no more than random removal. |
| Concept probes (CAV) | Held-out AUROC | 0.73 (tubules) to 0.87 (necrosis) | The concepts are partly learnable. This says nothing about model use. |
| Concept probes, external NCT data | Text and CAV AUROC | Lymphocytes: text 0.998, CAV 0.32 (inverted). Pleomorphism: 0.59 / 0.61 (weak). Necrosis: 0.939 / 0.952. Stroma/fat: 0.87 / 0.80 | The lymphocyte CAV points the wrong way. Pleomorphism barely transfers. |
| Concepts against BACH class | AUROC, invasive vs rest | Invasion 0.964, pleomorphism 0.949, tubules 0.08 (lower in invasive) | Association with the label, not evidence of causal use |
| Concept top-tile spot check | AI review (Claude Opus 5.5), not a pathologist | Strong: stroma/fat 20/20, invasion 19/20, tubules 18/20, pleomorphism 18/20. Mixed: duct-confined 12/20. Poor: lymphocytes 8/20, necrosis 3/20, mitoses 0/20, normal lobules 0/20 | Plausibility only, and not clinically reviewed |
| Cell features as a classifier | `cb_cells` | Cross-validation macro-F1 0.33 [0.26, 0.39]; test macro-F1 24.4 | Barely informative. Adding cells to text concepts lowers CV macro-F1 from 0.85 to 0.76. |
| Cell direction checks | Class means and pre-specified contrast | Contrast CI excludes 0 for `nuc_area_cv` 0.10 [0.06, 0.17] and `epi_fraction` 0.27 [0.09, 0.40]. Flat or opposite for `nuc_shape_cv` -0.01 [-0.01, 0.00], `neo_fraction` and `neo_density` (InSitu above Invasive) | Only two features behave as expected |
| Cell–concept agreement | Correlation | `nuc_area_cv` with pleomorphism: 0.34 (tile), 0.45 (case). `nuc_shape_cv` with pleomorphism: -0.04. `infl_fraction` with lymphocytes: 0.10 / 0.05 | Agreement only for nuclear area variability |
| Cell overlays | AI review | 15/21 acceptable | Segmentation quality unverified by a pathologist |

What can be claimed, and what cannot:

- **Tested and supported, weakly:** the region heatmap points to regions the production model depends on, more than random regions do. The effect is small.
- **Tested and not supported:** concept attributions as an explanation of the production model's output.
- **Not tested for faithfulness:** whether `cb_text` relies on the concepts it exposes. Retrieval, with precision@k of 0.67 [0.58, 0.83], is also not a faithfulness test.
- **Concepts to drop or relabel:** mitoses (0/20), normal lobules (0/20) and necrosis (3/20) should not be shown as tissue findings. Normal lobules is a clear example of a concept tracking context rather than the structure: its mean score is highest in Normal (1.47), yet none of its top tiles showed lobules. Lymphocytes should also be withheld until the inverted external result (CAV AUROC 0.32) is explained.
- All spot checks were done by AI reviewers, not pathologists.

## Weaknesses a reviewer will raise

| Criticism | What would address it |
|---|---|
| The test set is small (132 images, 24 groups, partly pseudo-patients), so four-class CIs span about 0.6–0.93 | An external, patient-labelled cohort, or at least the BACH WSI windows used as a second evaluation set |
| The conformal tier method was chosen after viewing test results, and the pre-registered LAC reached only 72.7% coverage | Lock the method, recalibrate on data that resembles the deployment distribution, and evaluate once on unseen data |
| Calibration was not shown to improve (NLL 0.56 to 0.66); the temperature was fit on train out-of-fold predictions, which are easier than test | Fit on held-out data that resembles test; report reliability diagrams and per-class calibration |
| Grouped cross-validation scores (macro-F1 0.951) are far above test (0.83), which points to a distribution shift between splits | Characterise the shift (stain, source, patients); report per-group errors |
| The deferral layer catches 46% of errors and the out-of-distribution signal is at chance (0.49) | Report abstention curves; drop or replace the out-of-distribution signal; test on real artifacts |
| Concept explanations failed the deletion test, and four of nine concepts failed the AI spot check | Faithfulness tests on `cb_text`; review by a pathologist; remove failed concepts from the interface |
| Cell features are near chance as a classifier and several direction checks are flat or reversed | Validate the segmentation against annotated nuclei before using cell features as explanations |
| The queue benefit is simulated; unflagged waits more than double (20.0 to 45.0 minutes); the aging guard has no measured effect; false negatives could not be measured | Model realistic read times and invasive cases that fall outside tiers 1–2; tune aging targets so they actually trigger within a day |
| The margin read is simulated from image borders and misses about half of carcinoma | Evaluate on real inked-margin material; state the trade-off between threshold and sensitivity |
| Robustness drops about 14 points at the mildest degradation | Add augmentation or QC gating for degraded inputs, and re-measure |
| The benchmark protocol differs from THUNDER | Re-run the published whole-image protocol under our setup |

## Next experiments

Ranked by expected value.

1. **Independent confirmation of the locked confidence pipeline.**
   - Freeze `aps_marginal_nonempty` and the temperature.
   - Recalibrate on a calibration set that resembles the test distribution, for example grouped out-of-fold predictions rather than the easy 50-image split.
   - Evaluate once on data not yet used for this purpose, such as the annotated BACH WSI windows.
   - Report coverage, set size, NLL and an abstention curve.
   - Value: this is the only way to turn the post-hoc 90.2% into evidence. It needs no new GPU work.
2. **Faithfulness tests for the concept model, and pruning of failed concepts.**
   - On `cb_text`, intervene on concept values (zero them or set them to class means) and measure the change in output.
   - Repeat region deletion at several deletion fractions and add insertion curves.
   - Remove mitoses, normal lobules and necrosis from the interface, and lymphocytes unless its inverted NCT result can be resolved.
   - Value: this moves the interpretability claim from "plausible" to "tested", or shows it is unsupported.
3. **Blinded pathologist review of the spot-check sets.**
   - Have a pathologist review the same 200 concept tiles and 21 cell overlays.
   - Measure agreement with the AI review.
   - Value: it replaces AI plausibility with expert judgement and shows whether the strong concepts really reach 18–20 of 20. It is feasible because the tile sets already exist.
